newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Colonial eyes card securitisation.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Colonial eyes card securitisation.

text.p: Australia's Colonial State Bank said on Monday it was not far away from entering the emerging credit card receivables securitisation market.
"I think it's quite likely that we will," Colonial State managing director, Stuart James, told a news conference.
He said Colonial State's possible entry into the market was less than a year way.
Earlier, Colonial State and RAMS, a home loan mortgage originator, jointly launched a co-branded Visa card, known as RAMS Visacard.
RAMS managing director John Kinghorn said RAMS was not interested in entering the securitisation of credit card receivables as RAMS preferred to specialise in the home mortgage market.
However, he said the sector was likely to boom in Australia as it has done in the United States.
"Securitisation of credit card receivables are the way of the future," Kinghorn said.
James agreed there was nothing stopping the sector growing strongly here.
"It's a pretty well travelled path in industry overseas," James said.
"There's no reason to assume that credit card receivables couldn't be dealt with in exactly the same way as mortgages," he said.
"In that sense, it's just the tip of the iceberg."

The development of a securitised mortgage market in the last three years has transformed the A$150 billion home mortgage market, with mortgage originators snaring about 10 percent of the market with cheaper interest rates than the major banks.
The banks had outstanding credit card advances of A$7.24 billion, as measured by the Reserve Bank of Australia at November 1996.
